class.name: NetwPredictionEngine
class.brief_description: The session's prediction engines, one pool keyed by an opaque slot.
class.description: A predicting entity's engine has identity and memory, and there is one per predicting entity rather than one per session. The pool is the registered object and the engines are rows in it, because registering a class per entity would hand a caller something that has to dissolve into slot-keyed storage later. A slot decides and never performs. It reads the facts a caller hands it, answers with a plan, and writes nothing outside itself: no node, no clock, no binding. That is what lets a transition be reproduced from its journal row alone, and it is why the caller stays responsible for reading colliders, calling a body and writing values back. [codeblock] slot = open(declaration) one slot per predicting entity configure(slot, ...) refused outside what supports() admits record_input / open_drive the pass a caller performs close_drive the row the pass produced admit_ack / compare_state what the far peer answered recover / quarantine_state the plan a caller then writes close(slot) the entity is gone [/codeblock] [method supports] is the flip axis. The pool declares which CONFIGURATIONS it can drive, a caller asks before handing it a tick, and outside the declared set [method configure] refuses rather than storing. There is never a mixed engine, so no per-region hop is paid at runtime. Every role is driven, because the pass a slot performs is the same one whichever peer owns the entity: a role decides whether a caller reaches the slot, never what the slot then does.

method.name: archetype_axes
method.description: The axis point a [enum NetwPredict.Archetype] declares, as the preset a body type implies rather than as a value a game repeated by hand. [codeblock] ┠╴declared false for NONE, which declares nothing ┠╴schedule a NetwPredict.Schedule value ┠╴missing_policy a NetwPredict.MissingInput value ┠╴recovery_policy a NetwPredict.RecoveryPolicy value ┠╴snap_restore a NetwPredict.RestoreMode value ┠╴declares_snap_restore false leaves the declared restore alone ┠╴teleport_threshold in the pose field's own units ┖╴declares_teleport_threshold false leaves the declared distance alone [/codeblock] An axis the archetype does not declare carries its [code]declares_[/code] flag as [code]false[/code], because an archetype names the axes its body type settles and leaves every other one as the game declared it. Reading a flagged-off value overwrites a game's own choice with a default it never asked for.

method.name: adopt_alignment
method.description: Records the alignment a shell staged: where it landed and that the fallback retires, without planning the payload. [method align_reseed] is the same bookkeeping for an alignment the pool planned itself.

method.name: apply_input
method.description: Writes the declared input fields [param payload] names onto the bound owner and answers whether the owner resolved.

method.name: apply_state
method.description: Writes the declared state fields [param payload] names onto the bound owner and answers whether the owner resolved. A key the declaration does not name is ignored.

method.name: attempt_carry
method.description: Runs this slot's rule for [param field] against every transition past [param basis] and answers what it produced with every probe it earned. The rule is replayed against one transition the owner already recorded before it is folded at all, so the fold's purity bracket only ever covers a rule the replay accepted. [param teleport_default] and [param divergence_epsilon] are the entity-wide fallbacks a field with no declared [code]teleport_at[/code] or [code]epsilon_override[/code] is judged at. They are handed in rather than held, because they are the caller's configuration and the pool decides against them rather than owning them. Answers evidence alone. [method judge_carry] turns it into a verdict, and [method decline_carry] is the refusal for an attempt with no evidence to judge.

method.name: bind_owner
method.description: Binds [param owner] as the object this slot reads declared input onto and captures declared state from, and answers whether the slot exists. The slot holds an id rather than a pointer and resolves it at each property-I/O moment, because the simulate step between them is arbitrary user code and may free the object. Binding is optional: a slot driven by [method set_state] alone never binds and touches no property. A callable named [code]_network_tick[/code] on [param owner] is adopted as [method set_simulate]'s step by convention; an explicit [method set_simulate] call always wins and keeps winning across a re-bind. Which declared fields the owner answers for is resolved here rather than per pass, because the declaration and the owner are both fixed once bound, so the answer cannot change without one of them changing.

method.name: bind_timeline
method.description: Adopts [param timeline] as the store this slot reads its input lane and its tick-keyed states out of. It is handed in rather than minted, because a server role shares one store with the recorder writing authority rows into it and two stores would be two histories that agree only by accident. The entry book [method entry_history] answers is minted here instead, because a FRAME transition is a tape entry rather than a tick and its states cannot be filed under a numbering the input lane also uses.

method.name: canonical_input_bytes
method.description: The wire bytes of [param payload]'s declared input fields, in declaration order.

method.name: canonical_state_bytes
method.description: The wire bytes of [param payload]'s declared state fields, in declaration order. The bytes that ship are the bytes that hash, so a fingerprint taken here and one taken by a peer decoding the frame describe the same values. Two payloads are comparable exactly when they name the same fields.

method.name: canonicalize_input
method.description: [param payload] with every declared input value round-tripped through its own codec, so both peers feed the simulation the same values.

method.name: canonicalize_state
method.description: [param payload] with every declared state value round-tripped through its own codec. A predicting peer and its authority never see the same float twice, one reads a live property and the other reads what survived the wire, so the round trip is what makes the two comparable exactly rather than approximately. A field with no quantizer round-trips through its raw wire form.

method.name: capture_input
method.description: The declared input fields the bound owner holds, read through the input declaration [method rewire] was given.

method.name: capture_state
method.description: The declared state fields the bound owner holds. A field the owner does not answer for is absent rather than null.

method.name: carry_eligible
method.description: Whether [param slot]'s carry rule for [param field] may still be invoked. Asked BEFORE the invocation: a rule the pool has already convicted must not be handed the game's own code to run one more time.

method.name: carry_judgeable
method.description: Whether a carry rule may be judged across [param transition], which needs BOTH of its ends to be the owner's own drive. A rule states what a DRIVE does, so judging it across a recorded state a recovery wrote would convict it of the engine's own correction. Mark those states with [method mark_carry_dirty].

method.name: coast_command
method.description: Every declared input field at the zero of its own DECLARED type, which is the command COAST is defined as. A field whose declaration carries no type is omitted rather than guessed, because the whole point of the row is that it commands nothing and a value invented for a type nobody declared is a command like any other. A declared colour zeroes to a transparent one rather than to [Color]'s own default of opaque black, so it coasts to nothing the way every other type does.

method.name: clear_out_of_domain_window
method.description: Drops [param slot]'s out-of-domain window, so [method out_of_domain_until] reads -1 again and [method out_of_domain_at] answers false for every label. A rewire re-keys the transitions a window was expressed in, so an open window cannot mean anything across one and is dropped rather than carried.

method.name: close
method.description: Retires [param slot] and everything it held. A key never comes back, so a caller holding a stale one reads an unopened slot rather than another entity's.

method.name: close_drive
method.description: [param post_fp] is the fingerprint of the state this transition ended at, which the next transition's pre-state fingerprint must equal or the chain between them is broken.

method.name: command_admit
method.description: Files one decoded owner cell and answers whether it was taken. A transition the window already holds answers [code]false[/code] and keeps the first arrival: the owner lane re-sends an overlapping window every frame, so a second arrival is that redundancy rather than a correction, and taking it would let a late duplicate rewrite a transition the consume cursor may already have passed.

method.name: command_depth_from
method.description: The contiguous decoded cells beginning exactly at [param cursor]. A hole ends the run, because the consume cursor may not step over a transition whose command has not arrived.

method.name: command_label_of
method.description: The input tick the owner labelled [param transition] with, or [code]-1[/code] for a transition the window does not answer for.

method.name: command_payload_of
method.description: The command the owner authored [param transition] with, empty for a transition the window does not answer for. It stays a [Dictionary] because it is keyed by the input set's own field names, which the pool never declares and cannot order.

method.name: command_transitions
method.description: Every decoded transition still held, ascending. The window gaps wherever a datagram was lost, so a caller enumerating it reads this rather than a range.

method.name: configure
method.description: Stores [param slot]'s configuration, or refuses when [method supports] answers false. Refused rather than stored, so a slot never holds an axis point its own pool declines to drive. The refusal is the return value and nothing else: this method answers [code]false[/code] and stores nothing rather than raising, so a caller that ignores the answer runs an entity the pool never configured.

method.name: correction_for_recovery_policy
method.description: The [enum NetwPredict.CorrectionMode] mechanism a [enum NetwPredict.RecoveryPolicy] runs through. A policy names a strategy and the mechanism is how it is carried out, so several policies share one mechanism without sharing a meaning. Only [constant NetwPredict.RecoveryPolicy.REBASE_REPLAY] runs through [constant NetwPredict.CorrectionMode.REPLAY]. [constant NetwPredict.RecoveryPolicy.OBSERVE] writes nothing at all, so the mechanism named for it only decides what the recovery would have run had it written.

method.name: converge_rate_of
method.description: [param slot]'s declared convergence stiffness for [param field], or [code]-1.0[/code] when the declaration named none.

method.name: declare_skipped
method.description: Journals [param transition] as one authority declared it never ran. A transition [param slot] never opened is sealed as a substitution, because a declared skip names exactly which command did not run where a silent gap is indistinguishable from a lost frame. One the slot did open is overlaid instead, so the evidence it already recorded stays readable behind the verdict that retired it.

method.name: dissipate_declared
method.description: Whether [param slot] declared a withheld momentum field. That field is the only thing a dissipate window lets go of, so a declaration with none can never open one.

method.name: drive_stats
method.description: [param slot]'s [enum NetwPredict.DriveStat] counters, kept as the decision already computed them so a shell or a plot never recomputes a drive.

method.name: entry_history
method.description: The FRAME tier's own state store, keyed by the transition each state stands BEFORE, so a transition's post-state and its successor's pre-state are one entry. A slot has one from the moment it opens, and [method tape_reset] mints a fresh one, because the entry index it is keyed by is injective only within a tape epoch. Nothing else replaces it: a caller holding the store must be able to write into the one the pool reads.

method.name: episode_active
method.description: Whether [param slot] is inside an episode. A scalar rather than a report, because a report copies the whole retained record and this is read once per guard.

method.name: episode_stats
method.description: [param slot]'s episode counters, one array a guard indexes rather than a report it would have to copy the retained record to read.

method.name: epsilon_of
method.description: [param slot]'s declared divergence epsilon for [param field], or [code]-1.0[/code] when the declaration named none.

method.name: escalation_field_of
method.description: Which declared field's divergence a recovery is answering, as an index into the declaration, or [code]-1[/code] when neither state carries one. Ranked by error over the field's OWN tolerance so fields in different units are comparable: a raw maximum would hand the answer to whichever field carries the larger numbers rather than to whichever is furthest out of tolerance. A field declaring a tolerance of zero triggers on any error and has no scale to be ranked on, so it ranks last and answers only when no field with a positive tolerance did. With nothing past its own tolerance the ranking falls back to raw magnitude, because the delta still has a sign the overshoot test is entitled to see.

method.name: escalation_pending
method.description: Whether [param slot]'s ladder has an escalation waiting. Read before a recovery is staged, because the transport attempt ahead of it declines on a promoted recovery.

method.name: field_slot
method.description: The slot [param key] was compiled to, or [code]-1[/code] when [param slot]'s declaration does not name it. A field's slot here is also its column on the wire, so this is the only place a field name is resolved to a number.

method.name: is_causal
method.description: Whether [param slot] declared [param field]'s property class as CAUSAL rather than DERIVED or COSMETIC, the same three-way split [code]NetwPropertySet.PropertyClass[/code] declares a property with.

method.name: is_open
method.description: Whether [param slot] names a live engine.

method.name: journal_basis_at
method.description: The write [method journal_operator_at] accounts for, or [code]-1[/code] when nothing wrote the body.

method.name: journal_has
method.description: Whether [param slot]'s journal still retains [param transition]. A transition nobody retained is one nobody can show was entitled to exactness, so a forgotten transition reads as false rather than as an error.

method.name: journal_last_closed
method.description: The frontier an acknowledgement may claim. An open row holds a zero fingerprint, so claiming it would assert a state no drive has produced.

method.name: journal_operator_at
method.description: The operator write that accounts for a state-chain discontinuity ahead of this row, or [code]0[/code] with [method journal_basis_at] at [code]-1[/code] when nothing wrote the body.

method.name: journal_post_families_at
method.description: Pose, momentum, then controller, the order every family fingerprint triple is written and read in.

method.name: journal_pre_families_at
method.description: Pose, momentum, then controller, the order every family fingerprint triple is written and read in.

method.name: journal_row
method.description: A row opens when [param transition] is authored and closes when its produced state is fingerprinted, so a closed row names one drive completely. Evidence is immutable after close while the verdict overlay, attribution and domain may settle later, which is what makes the fingerprint an acceptance test rather than a tolerance. A [param transition] the ring no longer retains reads as the label that claims nothing, since nobody retaining it can show it was entitled to exactness.

method.name: journal_slot_of
method.description: The ring index [param transition] occupies in [param slot]'s journal, or [code]-1[/code] when the ring no longer retains it. Every column reader addresses a ring index while a transition names a row rather than a position, so a caller holding a transition resolves it here once and indexes every column with the answer. The search runs newest first, since every caller addresses a recent transition.

method.name: journal_transition_at
method.description: [param index] runs oldest first, the order every journal column reader shares, so one index names the same row across all of them.

method.name: judge_carry
method.description: The pool's standing verdict on [param slot]'s carry rule for one field. Addressed by field NAME and resolved against the slot's own table, so no caller mints a second numbering for the fields.

method.name: mark_aligned_error
method.description: Records the aligned error of a comparison that reached a verdict. An unsettled comparison reached none, so the column stays unwritten rather than carrying a zero that would read as agreement.

method.name: mark_authority_ack
method.description: Records [param transition] as the frontier a caller proved on a lane the pool does not decode. A transition can be acknowledged without [param slot] ever holding a journal row for it, and the speculative span [method drive_stats] reports is measured from the freshest proof on either lane rather than from the newest row. The frontier never retreats: an older acknowledgement arriving after a newer one cannot reopen a horizon the newer one already closed.

method.name: mark_carry_dirty
method.description: Records that the state at [param transition] is something other than a drive result, so [method carry_judgeable] refuses the two transitions it bounds. A slot that declares no rule records nothing, because a book no rule can be judged against is a book nothing reads. The book is bounded with the tape it indexes into and a rewire empties it, because either way the marks it drops name transitions no rule can still reach.

method.name: mark_domain
method.description: Records the domain [param transition] ran in for [param slot]. The domain is the shell's answer. Whether an entity declared its world, whether it declared that world approximate, and how long a change to it keeps the window open are all facts the pool stores for nobody.

method.name: open
method.description: Opens a slot for one predicting entity and returns its key. The key is opaque: it is not an index, not a route and not an entity id, and nothing outside this pool may derive one.

method.name: open_count
method.description: How many engines the pool holds.

method.name: open_drive
method.description: Attempts one transition and answers the drive it produced. [method NetwPredictDrive.ran] false with [method NetwPredictDrive.held] or [method NetwPredictDrive.clamped] set is a refusal the pass earned rather than an error: the horizon was full, or a FRAME slot declined a tick that bought no simulated time. A predicting slot holds the horizon: it declines rather than opens once it has run more than one quarter of the history ring ahead of what authority has acknowledged, about one second at the standard rate, leaving the rest of the ring for acknowledgement and recovery evidence. A slot that is the authority for its own commands confirms nothing back to itself, so the horizon never applies to it. A FRAME slot also refuses a second frame at a tick it already transitioned, the same clamp as one that bought no simulated time. Input capture continues while the body holds, so the horizon bounds the speculation and never the command lane.

method.name: open_out_of_domain_window
method.description: Extends [param slot]'s out-of-domain window to [param cooldown] labels past [param label], never shortening one already open. A window opens on a fact that makes some antecedent unequal between the two peers: a contact against a body this peer does not simulate equivalently, an island roster that moved, or a world epoch the game bumped. It stays open a cooldown past that fact because the disturbance keeps perturbing the bodies after the frame that reported it, and while it is open [method NetwPredictionCore.domain_of] answers [constant NetwPredictJournal.Domain.OUT_OF_DOMAIN], which is what stops a divergence being charged to the solver.

method.name: order_key_of
method.description: [param slot]'s order key, the entity's ROUTE, the session-global integer identity that replicates to every peer, so two peers step the same roster in the same order without exchanging anything about it. Set with [method set_order_key].

method.name: ordered_slots
method.description: Every open slot, ascending by order key and then by slot, which is what makes the order total even before every slot has been keyed. An unkeyed slot sorts after every keyed one, and ties break on the slot itself.

method.name: out_of_domain_at
method.description: Whether [param slot]'s open out-of-domain window still covers [param label], which is the contact-window fact a recovery plan is judged under. False whenever no window is open, so a caller never has to test [method out_of_domain_until] against -1 itself.

method.name: out_of_domain_until
method.description: The label [param slot]'s open out-of-domain window stops covering, and -1 when none is open. This is the window argument [method NetwPredictionCore.domain_of] reads. Opened by [method open_out_of_domain_window] and dropped by [method clear_out_of_domain_window]. [method out_of_domain_at] is the same fact asked about one label.

method.name: owner_bound
method.description: Whether [param slot] currently holds a live owner.

method.name: owner_solves
method.description: Whether [param slot]'s bound owner solves its own transition, a physics body rather than a scripted step. Answered at the bind rather than asked per correction, because it is a fact about the object and the object does not change class.

method.name: pass_depth
method.description: How deep a pass is currently running, and zero when none is. Nonzero is what the roster verbs refuse against, so a step cannot open, close, rewire or re-bind a slot the pass is walking.

method.name: pass_slots
method.description: The slots phase [param phase] steps, in the pool's declared order. Order and participation are both determinism contracts: two peers step the same roster in the same order without exchanging anything about it, and a slot the phase does not name is one the phase must not reach. The BODY stays with the caller, so this answers a list rather than driving one, and no phase pays a call back across the language boundary per slot.

method.name: pending_provenance
method.description: The last out-of-transition body write staged against [param slot], stamped onto the next row the slot opens so that row records what moved the body before it ran. Empty once the row it belongs to has been opened, because a write is provenance for one transition and inventing a second would exonerate a solver that ran unperturbed. Set with [method set_pending_provenance] and read by [method mark_provenance].

method.name: projection_of
method.description: [param slot]'s compiled projection for [param field], read back under the name the GDScript wiring spells it with, because the certification arm compares the two.

method.name: record_breach
method.description: Records that [param transition] is the contact that demoted [param slot] out of speculation. The detail stays with the caller that sampled it; the pool records only which transition.

method.name: record_episode_decision
method.description: Charges a conditional operator's verdict against [param slot]'s episode. The pool decides admissibility; only the caller that gathered the evidence knows whether the corridor it then ran agreed, so the verdict is recorded here rather than inferred.

method.name: record_evidence
method.description: A solve that woke into [param transition] is one the solver started rather than continued, so [param sleeping] tells the pool the previous solve's rest state has to survive it.

method.name: record_idle_drive
method.description: Records a pass that advanced the lane without opening a transition: a hold, a starve, or a substituted command. It counts as a drive because a reader asking when [param slot] last acted is asking about these too, and it opens no journal row because nothing was simulated.

method.name: refresh_ack_age
method.description: Recomputes [constant STAT_ACK_AGE_TICKS] from the freshest acknowledgement. [method open_drive] already refreshes it before authoring the entry it is about to open, so a caller reading the span after a drive reads it as of that drive's start; this is for reading it at any other moment.

method.name: replay_drive
method.description: Journals a transition whose fold has already been decided, so the caller names [param transition], [param label] and [param kind] instead of reading them back. Two callers want that, and [param authoring] is what tells them apart. A consuming peer re-runs a lane its owner numbered: the tape entry arrived with the entry, so nothing here may author one, and every queued entry replays at one timing where [method open_drive] would admit only the first. An owner on a tick schedule instead knows its own answers before it asks, because a tick drive is its own transition and every entry is fresh; passing [code]true[/code] makes this advance the tape and the input cursor exactly as [method open_drive] would have, and the transition it answers is the tape's, not the caller's. [param authoring] does nothing on a [constant NetwPredict.Schedule.FRAME] slot, where the tape entry IS the fold and only [method open_drive] can decide it.

method.name: replay_entries
method.description: Every transition this slot drove after [param basis], oldest first. The pool composes them out of the tape and the input lane it holds, so a replay and a carry are handed one account rather than each rebuilding one. FRAME numbers a transition by its tape entry, so an entry the clock repeated carries the command the last fresh entry authored: the owner ran that sample again rather than authoring a new one. Every other tier numbers a transition by its tick and reads the command filed under it, whether or not the owner recorded one there. [param basis] seeds the carry from the command the basis entry itself ran, so the first repeated entry past it is not left empty.

method.name: resolve_correction
method.description: The correction mode [param slot] resolves [param declared] to. [constant NetwPredict.CORRECTION_AUTO] earns a snap only from a solver body, whose transition is a physics step and cannot be re-run per input. A slot with no owner replays.

method.name: rewire
method.description: Recompiles [param slot]'s field tables from [param declaration] and its input codec from [param input]. Both declarations are read here and never retained, so a caller may reuse and refill one. Each field's name and declared property type resolve to a table index here, once, rather than at every later read: a recovery reading many field-keyed tables afterward pays one index lookup per field per tick rather than a hash lookup. [param input] compiles to a codec and nothing else, because an input row is canonicalized and shipped and never recovered, so it earns no recovery tables. Rewiring without one forgets the previous input codec.

method.name: role_for_axes
method.description: The [enum NetwPredict.Role] named by a [enum NetwPredict.InputSource] and a [enum NetwPredict.SimMode]. The axes are the decision and the role is its name, so every role is reachable from some pair and no pair reaches a role that contradicts it. [codeblock] AUTHORITATIVE SPECULATIVE DISPLAY LOCAL HOST_LOCAL PREDICT REMOTE RECEIVED CONSUME (unreachable) REMOTE PREDICTED (unreachable) SIMULATE REMOTE NONE REMOTE REMOTE REMOTE [/codeblock] The simulation axis is asked first, because a peer running no simulation needs no command, so where it would have read one cannot change what it is. The two unreachable pairs answer [constant NetwPredict.Role.REMOTE] rather than refusing, so a caller reading a role always has one.

method.name: role_of
method.description: The role [param slot] was configured with.

method.name: run_step
method.description: One authored transition, run on [param slot]'s bound owner. The declared input is applied through the port, the step runs, and the declared state is captured back, which is the whole of what a pass does to a game object. The roster is FROZEN for the duration: a step that opens, closes, rewires or re-binds a slot is refused and counted, so a speculative game act during a fresh tick goes through an effect rather than through the roster.

method.name: sample_environment
method.description: Runs every sensor [method set_sensor] declared and folds what they answered, with [param epoch], into this transition's world digest. What they answered is held for [method sensor_samples]. A slot that names no epoch and declares no sensor digests to the same zero an unwritten row already holds, so the fold is skipped rather than run to reach a foregone answer. Every drive of every predicting entity passes through here. The sensors run inside the pass, so one that tries to open or close a slot is refused exactly as a step is.

method.name: schedule_of
method.description: The schedule [param slot] was configured with.

method.name: sensor_samples
method.description: What the declared sensors answered on the last [method sample_environment]. Held rather than re-sampled, so a caller reading one world fact reads the value the digest was taken over rather than a fresher one the transition never saw.

method.name: set_order_key
method.description: Sets the key [param slot] is stepped under. The pass order is a determinism contract rather than a convenience: two peers step the same roster the same way or their transitions are not comparable.

method.name: set_pending_provenance
method.description: Stages the write [param slot]'s next opened row is stamped with, or clears the staging when [param provenance] is empty. See [method pending_provenance].

method.name: set_simulate
method.description: The step behaviour [param slot] runs, one [Callable] per slot per role. An explicit simulate always wins over the one [method bind_owner] adopted by convention, and keeps winning across a re-bind, because a caller that named the step said something the convention cannot override.

method.name: state_before
method.description: The declared state [param transition] ran FROM, out of the book its tier keys by, which is [method entry_history] under FRAME and the bound timeline otherwise. Empty where the book holds no entry, which is the absence a caller judging a rule across the pair already handles.

method.name: stamp_pending_provenance
method.description: Writes [param slot]'s staged write onto row [param transition] through [method mark_provenance], and does nothing when nothing is staged. See [method pending_provenance] for what a caller stages there. A row a write explains is not a chain break: the drive that opened it already flagged the discontinuity between its own starting state and the state the row before it closed at, and stamping the write that caused the discontinuity retires the flag. So a caller stamps before it reads the row's flags, and a transition nobody wrote through keeps the break it earned.

method.name: state_family_of
method.description: The state family [param slot] compiled [param field] into, crossing as a plain int: [code]0[/code] POSE, [code]1[/code] MOMENTUM, [code]2[/code] CONTROLLER. The family decides what a recovery may write to the field.

method.name: slot_bind_owner
method.description: Binds [param owner] to the row [param entity] is keyed to, resolving at bind time what the owner can answer for. Returns [code]false[/code] when [param entity] holds no row.

method.name: slot_of
method.description: The row [param entity] is keyed to, or [code]-1[/code]. The entity is held as a plain [RefCounted] and keyed by its instance id, so the pool never needs the entity's own type. This map and the row store erase each other, so a row cannot outlive its key.

method.name: slot_register
method.description: Mints the row [param entity] is keyed to and returns it, or returns the existing row when one is already keyed. One registered engine holds N slot-keyed rows rather than one object per predicting entity, so registering does not hand GDScript a per-entity class to name.

method.name: slot_registered
method.description: How many entities currently hold a row.

method.name: slot_unbind_owner
method.description: Drops the owner bound by [method slot_bind_owner], leaving the row itself registered.

method.name: slot_unregister
method.description: Releases the row [param entity] is keyed to and erases the key. A later [method slot_of] answers [code]-1[/code].

method.name: state_fingerprint
method.description: The fingerprint of [param payload] narrowed to the fields [param slot] declared CAUSAL, which is the only scope a comparison judges: a recovery restores fields the comparison has no business reading, so fingerprinting the whole payload would make an agreeing transition read as a fork. The result is SIGNED, because that is the width the journal columns and the wire both carry, so a fingerprint never changes representation between being computed, stored and sent. Returns [code]0[/code] for a slot that holds no row.

method.name: state_family_fingerprints
method.description: The same causal scope as [method state_fingerprint], split into the three state families and fingerprinted separately, always three entries in the order POSE, MOMENTUM, CONTROLLER, matching [method state_family_of]. A family names which PART of the state forked, so it only names a part the next transition reads. A family no causal field belongs to reports [code]0[/code] rather than the fingerprint of an empty payload, so a reader can tell an absent family from an agreeing one.

method.name: supports
method.description: Whether the pool can drive this CONFIGURATION. Ask before handing a slot a tick: [method configure] refuses what this declines, so a caller that skips the question fails silently per entity rather than loudly. Two configurations are refused for naming something no path performs. AUTO is a body-type guess and the body is what a slot cannot see. EXTRAPOLATED under REPLAY promises a projection, where REPLAY reaches the present by re-running commands over an exact restore.

method.name: tape_author
method.description: Appends one tape entry at the next entry index, for a pass that carries the owner command lane without opening a transition. A drive authors its own entry, so calling this beside one appends twice.

method.name: tape_label_of
method.description: The input tick the entry at [param index] was authored under, or [code]-1[/code] when the entry has fallen out of the ring, which is the same absence a caller reading past the horizon already handles.

method.name: tape_prepare_tick
method.description: Re-keys the tape to [param tick], opening a new epoch and dropping the ring when [param tick] is not contiguous with the newest entry, because the lane codec implies contiguous indices. Pairs with [method tape_author] for a pass that authors a command without opening a transition. A drive re-keys its own.

method.name: tape_reset
method.description: Opens [param epoch] and clears everything the previous one held. A transition is injective only within a tape epoch, so a journal outliving its epoch would hold two rows claiming one transition; that injectivity is the invariant a tape epoch exists to protect. The journal is re-keyed with it, so a transition the previous epoch held is one the new epoch has not seen, whatever its number. The bound input lane is untouched: it is keyed by tick rather than by tape entry and is shared with whatever else records into it, so a reset of this slot's transitions must not drop it.

method.name: tape_span
method.description: The oldest and newest entry index the ring still holds, both [code]-1[/code] when it holds nothing. A caller walks the tape over this range rather than over a count, because the ring drops its oldest entries and the indices it keeps are the recent ones. A slot the pool does not recognize answers the same absence, so a caller never walks a live entity's range by mistake.

method.name: teleport_of
method.description: [param slot]'s declared teleport threshold for [param field], or [code]-1.0[/code] when the declaration named none.

method.name: trigger_shape_of
method.description: Whether [param field_errors], in declaration order, ask for a recovery, and whether any field asking is one a sub-teleport restore may write. The answer is a [enum NetwPredict.TriggerShape]. A field's own declared epsilon outranks [param fallback_epsilon], an error the array does not hold asks for nothing, and a shape of [code]ALL_WITHHELD[/code] is the write that repairs nothing and is charged as non-contraction.

method.name: transport_admissible
method.description: Whether [param slot] admits a transport correction for what the caller sampled. The slot supplies the correction axis it was configured with, so a caller states only its sample.

method.name: trim_history
method.description: Retires everything the acknowledged transition [param ack] made unreachable, in whichever numbering this slot's schedule keeps its history under. FRAME acknowledges a tape entry, so it retires [method entry_history] at that index and the bound timeline at the label the entry authored, which are two numberings for one transition. Every other schedule numbers both by the tick.

method.name: unbind_owner
method.description: Releases [param slot]'s owner. The slot keeps deciding, it stops touching properties.

method.name: witness_judged
method.description: True once authority has answered for [param transition]'s witness. A solve the body slept through witnessed nothing, and one that woke into it witnessed a transition the solver started rather than continued, so neither is evidence a conditional operator may build on; this answers only whether a verdict has arrived, distinct from whether that verdict differs.

method.name: witness_row_clean
method.description: Whether [param transition]'s witness is evidence an operator may build on: awake through the whole solve, and reporting only contact the closure reproduces, which is nothing, the declared support, or static geometry. [param require_peer] additionally demands that authority witnessed the same thing, which is what makes the row a shared fact rather than a local one.

constants.constant: Incremented by [method tape_reset], which re-keys every other cursor to the new epoch too, because a retained position would name a transition the new epoch is about to reuse.
The tick a FRAME transition ran at. A second frame at this tick is refused, and it is not the transition the entry was authored at.

Charged when a drive's declared quantum undercounts the physics frames it actually advanced, so the peer integrated its solver by an amount no transition names and a comparison against it carries an error nothing can attribute.
